title: Amherst vs Williams: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: Amherst College (Amherst) versus Williams College (Williams). Also searched as Williams vs Amherst. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Amherst College and Williams College are both private nonprofit institutions located in Massachusetts, with Amherst situated in the town of Amherst and Williams in Williamstown. Amherst has an undergraduate enrollment of 1,911 students, while Williams enrolls slightly more, with 2,076 undergraduates. Tuition at Amherst is $70,480, which is marginally higher than Williams' tuition of $68,560. These differences highlight some of the distinctions between Amherst vs Williams in terms of size and cost.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Amherst College vs Williams College in terms of cost, Amherst's tuition is $70,480 for both in-state and out-of-state students, slightly higher than Williams College's tuition of $68,560. Despite the close tuition rates, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs, with Amherst graduates carrying a median debt of $13,740, while Williams graduates have a slightly lower median debt of $12,761. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments associated with attending each institution and are useful for prospective students evaluating Amherst vs Williams.

The campuses of both institutions provide environments conducive to close faculty-student interaction and collaborative learning, reflecting their commitment to personalized education. These aspects are central when considering Amherst College vs Williams College, as the learning experience is shaped by both enrollment size and campus setting.

sections.heading: Accreditation
paragraphs: Amherst College and Williams College are both accredited institutions, ensuring they meet established standards of quality in higher education.
